title: Longer LR anneal: WARMDOWN_RATIO 0.5 -> 0.8
description: One line in the hyperparameter block: WARMDOWN_RATIO 0.5 -> 0.8, so the LR multiplier is flat for the first 20% of the time budget and decays linearly to zero over the last 80% instead of the last 50%. Nothing else changed.
reflection: val_bpb 0.988189 | 488.9M tokens | 1865 steps | MFU 34.51% | VRAM 45.0GB | FLOPs/token 2.1077e8 | queued_s 687. Lowest raw number in the cell, but the honest effect is ~-0.0006, about 1 sd, and it is n=1 against an n=2 control. Scoring: control is a2's //8 pair (0.990541 @474.7M, 0.988725 @490.2M; mean 0.989633 @482.4M). My tokens (488.9M) sit essentially on top of the better control half (490.2M), so the least-assumption comparison is raw against that half: -0.00054. Corrected to the control mean's 482.4M at either published slope (-1.28e-4 or -1.17e-4 per 1M): -0.00062 to -0.00069. My pre-registered prediction was 0.9880 +/- 0.0010 and the falsifier was >=0.9896 corrected; I landed at 0.98902 corrected, so the axis is alive but the effect is the same ~0.0006 size as the window increments, not the bigger move I hoped for. What is genuinely established: (1) this is the cleanest contrast in the cell so far - FLOPs/token, MFU, VRAM and step count are all unchanged, so for once none of the delta can be tokens, and the same is not true of any window result; (2) a ~20% cut in integrated LR (mean multiplier 0.75 -> 0.60) costs nothing, which independently confirms a0's finding that the LR-magnitude axis is flat below 0.04 - the gain here is schedule shape, not step size. What it does NOT establish: 0.8 being optimal. The direction is now known and one bracketing run (0.65 or 1.0) would locate it, but at ~0.0006 per probe I would not spend two of the remaining slots on it.
